Bulluck''' (born April 4, 1977) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for eleven seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). (Ann Arbor, Michigan) | college = [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan]] | draftyear = 1983 | draftround = 2 | draftpick = 42 | pastteams = * [[Houston Oilers]] ({{NFL Year|1983|1988}}) * [[Indianapolis Colts]] ({{NFL Year|1989}})* * [[Cleveland Browns]] ({{NFL Year|1990}}) | highlights = * [[Pro Bowl]] (1987) * Second-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] ([[1982 College Football All-America Team|1982]]) * First-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten]] ([[1982 All-Big Ten Conference football team|1982]]) * 2× Second-team All-Big Ten ([[1980 All-Big Ten Conference football team|1980]], [[1981 All-Big Ten Conference football team|1981]]) | statlabel1 = [[Quarterback sack|Sacks]] | statvalue1 = 17.0 | statlabel2 = [[Interception]]s | statvalue2 = 13 | statlabel3 = [[Fumble|Fumble recoveries]] | statvalue3 = 7 | pfr = BostKe00 }} '''William Keith Bostic''' (born January 17, 1961) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for seven seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Bostic earned one [[Pro Bowl]] selection and missed another based on a tiebreaker for the last safety chosen. In his Pro Bowl season, he led the [[American Football Conference]] in [[interception]]s. Prior to playing in the NFL, he played for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]] of the [[Big Ten Conference]] from [[1979 NCAA Division I-A football season|1979]]–[[1982 NCAA Division I-A football season]]. During this time Michigan won two Big Ten championships, and Bostic was named first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten]]. While at Michigan, he accumulated [[fumble]] recovery and interception statistics that continue to rank among the leaders in school history. Bostic had a reputation as a very physical safety.

He is the former [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) [[Football Championship Subdivision]] (FCS, called I-AA at the time) record holder for career rushing yards per game and [[point (American football)|points]] per game.  He also established the FCS record for back-to-back games total rushing yards.  He continues to hold numerous [[Ivy League]] and Princeton Tigers rushing and scoring records.

Elias was signed as a [[free agent]] out of college by the [[New York Giants]] where he played from [[1994 NFL season|1994]] through [[1996 NFL season|1996]].  He served mostly on [[American football positions#Special teams|special teams]].  He last played in the NFL two seasons with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in [[1998 NFL season|1998]] and [[1999 NFL season|1999]].
